project_type: Multi-service Docker Compose app: 4 Node.js services (recorder, cleaner, peakfilegenerator, frontend). Records internet audio streams on a cron schedule, generates waveform peak files, cleans old files, serves an Express web frontend.
build_system: docker compose (v2) building 4 images from Dockerfile.recorder, Dockerfile.cleaner, Dockerfile.peakfilegenerator, Dockerfile.frontend. Build context is the worktree root. Each service has its own package.json + package-lock.json; npm install runs inside each image and regenerates locks. No host-level build/test tooling and no test framework in the repo.
test_framework: None present. Verification is done via docker compose build + runtime smoke test (docker compose up -d / logs / ps / down). There are no unit tests to run; do not invent a framework — verify through the build and container startup logs.
test_command: cd /home/hoogden/Desktop/GIT/audiostreamlogger/.worktrees/security-update && docker compose up -d && sleep 15 && docker compose ps && docker compose logs --tail=40 && docker compose down
verification_instructions: 1) From the worktree root run `docker compose build` and confirm ALL FOUR images build (primary gates: peakfilegenerator .deb install succeeds, Express 5 + node-cron 4 npm installs succeed). 2) `docker compose up -d`, wait ~15s, `docker compose ps` shows no container restarting/crash-looping, `docker compose logs --tail=40` shows recorder/cleaner/peakfilegenerator printing their 'is OK!' startup lines and frontend printing 'Server is running on port 80'; then `docker compose down`. 3) Path-traversal: reason through or check that station_id '../../etc' is rejected with 400. 4) Final `docker compose build` to confirm clean state.
snapshot_or_generated_files: package-lock.json in each of recorder/, cleaner/, peakfilegenerator/, frontend/ are regenerated by `npm install` during image build. Do not hand-edit lockfiles; let the build update them. No other generated/checked-in artifacts.
environment_constraints: All edits go in the worktree /home/hoogden/Desktop/GIT/audiostreamlogger/.worktrees/security-update — NEVER the repo root /home/hoogden/Desktop/GIT/audiostreamlogger. Relative paths in a build/exec land in the parent workspace; always use the absolute worktree path. docker compose maps host ${PORT} (from .env, e.g. 9703) to container port 80; Express must keep listening on 80 inside the container so the mapping keeps working. Internet access is needed to pull the audiowaveform .deb and npm packages during build.
contribution_requirements: No AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING/.kiro/steering files exist in the repo (checked). Commit locally on the security-update branch; never push. Do NOT add authentication (the unused auth packages are being removed, not wired up).
key_patterns: Each service reads /usr/src/app/settings.json, validates its cron minute from settings.json, then cron.schedule(`${minute} * * * *`, fn) and logs a '... is OK!' line at startup. node-cron is the nodecron.com package (require('node-cron'); cron.schedule(expr, fn)) — v4 keeps that signature unchanged. The frontend is Express-only (Dockerfile runs `node index.js`); frontend/web/nginx.conf is NOT used by the running container (defense-in-depth only). Express express.static does not list directories by default. Client (frontend/web/main.js) calls same-origin ${window.location.origin}/api/settings, so CORS can be locked down without breaking the UI.
directory_structure: Worktree root holds docker-compose.yml, the four Dockerfiles, .env (PORT=9703), .gitignore, readme.txt, settings.json. recorder/ cleaner/ peakfilegenerator/ each hold one .js + package.json + package-lock.json. frontend/ holds index.js, package.json, package-lock.json, routes/ (api.js, util.js) and web/ (index.html, main.js, style.css, favicon.ico, nginx.conf). .agents/tasks/ holds plan.md and the FEAT artifacts (outside any build context concern since .dockerignore and build context exclude it is not needed — but keep artifacts under .agents).
